## What is still open

- Maya is waiting on you in #247: she'll approve once CI is green, but wants the number of Orbitly events lost since #240 for Thursday's Orbitly call. Your replay run gives it: about 1.18M legitimate events dropped (≈8.1% of their iOS volume), with 4,352 genuine replays excluded [2][1].
- After #247 is merged and deployed, run the replay from landing for Orbitly (from 13/11 09:40 UTC) and for Zest (3,812 events lost). Then check that `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total{project="prj_0rb1"}` stays near zero. Landing keeps 30 days, so the data is still there [1].
- Before Friday's incident review (20/11), you owe an alert for when the dead-letter queue goes above 1,000 messages [7].
- The note asking the iOS team to restore UUIDs for `event_id` in 3.2.1 is drafted but not sent [1].

## What changed

- Maya's review and CI status on #247 are the only open point there. Nothing else on it has moved [2].
- Noa published the final postmortem for #233 and will present it on Friday [3].

## What you did

- You traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop, which Rachel relayed from their PM, to your own #240 dedupe. kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends `event_id` as a per-session counter, so distinct events from different devices collided. You then opened #247, which keys the dedupe on project, device and event_id [1].
